sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Media is considered the ______ institution of democracy; the government is run by ______.
State true or false: (i) Mass media have a strict code of conduct like doctors. (ii) Media can change people's attitudes and habits.
Name any two ethical codes for media persons.
questions.answer: Accuracy, confidentiality, protection of sources, right to privacy (any two).

questions.q: Match: (i) Legislature (ii) Executive (iii) Judiciary with (a) Supreme Court (b) Parliament (c) Prime Minister.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by 'global village'?
questions.answer: The whole world is shrinking and becoming like a village because media bring people closer through live events and the internet.

questions.q: Name the three institutions of a modern democratic government.
How do mass media promote distribution of goods?
questions.answer: Through advertising, media inform people about products, services and prices.

questions.q: Why is 'protection of sources' an ethical code?
questions.answer: Revealing a confidential source may harm that person, so media must never disclose the source.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the role of mass media in society.
questions.answer: Media inform and educate the people, change attitudes and habits (polio, HIV/AIDS), act as a bridge between government and public, bring the world closer, support trade through advertising and entertain.

questions.q: Elucidate any three ethical principles that media professionals should follow.
questions.answer: Accuracy: verify facts before publishing. Right to privacy: do not report on the private life of ordinary citizens. No incitement to violence or communal writing: do not provoke violence or communal problems.

questions.q: List any three positive and any three negative effects of media.
questions.answer: Positive: informs and educates, helps democracy, promotes trade. Negative: harms traditional culture, promotes violence, creates desire for non-essential products.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the relationship between mass media and democracy.
questions.answer: Legislature, Executive and Judiciary run government; media are the bridge, informing people about government decisions and bringing public reactions to the government, hence the fourth institution; government agencies under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting use media for policies.

questions.q: What are media ethics? List the ethical codes to be practised by media persons.
questions.answer: Media ethics are guidelines on right and wrong for media persons because they are powerful. Codes: accuracy, confidentiality, protection of sources, right to privacy, no incitement to violence, no vulgarity or obscenity and no communal writing; the Press Council of India issues guidelines.
